items.quote: I will tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know we are starving; so they have left the camp to hide in the countryside, thinking, ‘They will surely come out, and then we will take them alive and get into the city.’
items.contrast: The Arameans are the supposed planners; the starving Israelites are the people they intend to take alive.
items.reason: The king identifies the Arameans as “they,” then voices their supposed thought using “we.” Resolving the nested pronouns distinguishes the actors from their intended captives.
